summary: Knowledge-base category suggestions are now profile-led and fine-grained. The owner found them too broad and unrelated to the profile: OpenAlex topics and wide Louvain communities split one research line (world models) into robotics/multimodal/GAN groups. New app/organization_facets.py builds top categories from the current project's pinned profile terms (title or abstract mention, at least 2 papers; a term whose papers mostly sit inside a wider term nests under it; near-duplicate terms merge and are reported) and sub-categories from phrases repeated across titles inside each category (at most 6). Papers no pinned term covers are grouped by shared title phrases. Matching never crosses clause punctuation (a period inside a name such as Qwen2.5 is not a break); terms with Chinese characters match only their exact text or the English of an exact glossary name; terms over the 12-category limit are reported. Profile terms reach the worker on stdin (ASCII-escaped JSON), never argv. Suggest-apply nests children under their parent. The toolbar loses the refresh button; undo names the change it undoes (labels stored in a new nullable org_events.label column, added after a private backup) and layout saves no longer occupy undo; undoing a delete restores that category's layout. Louvain/NetworkX remain only for the relation graph.
scope_note: The worktree is shared with the uncommitted 2026-10-01-assistant-composer unit (app/static/index.html, tests/test_ui_layout.py and its change/evidence files); both units add a section to docs/HANDOFF.md. Commit them separately. tests/test_broad_organization.py is deleted because the broad OpenAlex-topic mode it covered was removed.

budget_impact.rationale: Suggestions stay offline and deterministic: local lexical matching over saved titles/abstracts and the local profile, no provider, prompt, network or gateway call.
budget_impact.before: Zero model tokens per suggestion run (TF-IDF + Louvain + OpenAlex topic labels from stored metadata).
budget_impact.after: Zero model tokens per suggestion run (pinned-term and title-phrase matching).
budget_impact.developer_usage: No paid calls. The browser preview's data directory holds a configured key, but only the knowledge base and suggestions were exercised.

checks.note: Run in the owner's terminal because the agent sandbox blocks localhost binds; the evidence file also records the node tests.

reviews.reviewer: Implementing agent; checked suggestions for a project with and without pinned terms in the browser preview, applied them, and checked nesting and the undo button.

Separate code-reviewer subagent (an agent, not the owner). First pass: no blocking bugs, seven issues (clause-crossing matches, mixed Chinese terms, undo of delete losing layout, migration without backup, O(n^2) phrase membership, unbounded interest terms, silently dropped terms) plus minor items, all fixed with regression tests. Second pass: FAIL on a regression (version numbers such as Qwen2.5 split as clauses) and a minor unclassified-fold issue; both fixed with tests. Third pass: VERDICT PASS.

open_risks: Grouping quality is checked only on the owner's world-model library and synthetic fixtures; other disciplines and very long titles are unmeasured.
Timing at 2000 papers was measured once on synthetic random-vocabulary text (about 2.6-3.2 s), not on a real large library.
A named undo discards an open suggestions preview (existing behaviour).
After a named undo, a node position removed by a later layout save can reappear (reviewer: rare, non-blocking); a same_as note can name a term that was itself dropped over the limit.
The legacy regroup apply mode creates only top-level categories, never children.
Verified in the Chromium preview; the .app WKWebView needs the owner's look. Owner review of the migration (critical path) is pending.
